N1.text: Order positive/negative integers, decimals and fractions; use =, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥

N2.text: Four operations (formal written methods) on integers, decimals, fractions and mixed numbers, positive and negative; place value

N3.text: Inverse operations, priority of operations incl. brackets, powers, roots and reciprocals

N4.text: Primes, factors, multiples, common factors/multiples, HCF, LCM, prime factorisation, product notation

N5.text: Systematic listing strategies incl. the product rule for counting

N6.text: Positive integer powers and real roots; powers of 2, 3, 4, 5; estimate powers and roots

N7.text: Calculate with roots, and with integer and fractional indices

N8.text: Calculate exactly with fractions, surds and multiples of π; simplify surds; rationalise denominators

N9.text: Calculate with and interpret standard form A × 10ⁿ, 1 ≤ A < 10

N10.text: Work interchangeably with terminating decimals and fractions; recurring decimals ↔ fractions

N11.text: Identify and work with fractions in ratio problems

N12.text: Interpret fractions and percentages as operators

N13.text: Use standard units of mass, length, time, money and other measures, incl. compound measures

N14.text: Estimate answers; check calculations using approximation and estimation, incl. answers obtained using technology

N15.text: Round to an appropriate degree of accuracy; use inequality notation for error intervals due to truncation or rounding

N16.text: Apply and interpret limits of accuracy, incl. upper and lower bounds

A1.text: Use and interpret algebraic notation (ab, 3y, a², a/b, brackets, fractional coefficients)

A2.text: Substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions, incl. scientific formulae

A3.text: Understand vocabulary: expressions, equations, formulae, identities, inequalities, terms, factors

A4.text: Simplify and manipulate algebraic expressions: collecting like terms, expanding brackets, factorising (incl. quadratics, difference of two squares), algebraic fractions, laws of indices

A5.text: Use standard formulae; rearrange formulae to change the subject

A6.text: Equation vs identity; argue mathematically; use algebra to support and construct arguments and proofs

A7.text: Interpret expressions as functions; inverse and composite functions (formal notation expected)

A8.text: Work with coordinates in all four quadrants

A9.text: Plot straight-line graphs; y = mx + c; parallel and perpendicular lines; equation through two points or a point with a gradient

A10.text: Identify and interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions, graphically and algebraically

A11.text: Identify roots, intercepts and turning points of quadratics graphically; deduce roots algebraically and turning points by completing the square

A12.text: Recognise, sketch and interpret graphs of linear, quadratic, simple cubic, reciprocal, exponential and trigonometric functions

A13.text: Sketch translations and reflections of a given function

A14.text: Plot and interpret graphs (incl. reciprocal, exponential, non-standard) in real contexts, e.g. kinematics

A15.text: Calculate or estimate gradients and areas under graphs (incl. non-linear); interpret for distance-time, velocity-time and financial graphs

A16.text: Equation of a circle centred at the origin; equation of a tangent at a given point

A17.text: Solve linear equations in one unknown (incl. unknown on both sides); approximate solutions using a graph

A18.text: Solve quadratic equations by factorising, completing the square and the quadratic formula; approximate solutions using a graph

A19.text: Solve two simultaneous equations (linear/linear or linear/quadratic) algebraically; approximate solutions using a graph

A20.text: Find approximate solutions to equations numerically using iteration

A21.text: Translate situations into algebraic expressions/formulae; derive and solve equations and interpret solutions

A22.text: Solve linear inequalities (one or two variables) and quadratic inequalities; solution sets on number line, with set notation and on a graph

A23.text: Generate terms of a sequence from term-to-term or position-to-term rules

A24.text: Recognise and use triangular, square, cube numbers, arithmetic progressions, Fibonacci, quadratic sequences and geometric progressions

A25.text: Deduce expressions for the nth term of linear and quadratic sequences

R1.text: Change freely between related standard units and compound units (speed, rates of pay, prices, density, pressure) in numerical and algebraic contexts

R2.text: Use scale factors, scale diagrams and maps

R3.text: Express one quantity as a fraction of another (fraction < or > 1)

R4.text: Use ratio notation, including reduction to simplest form

R5.text: Divide a quantity in a part:part or part:whole ratio; apply ratio to real contexts (conversion, comparison, scaling, mixing, concentrations)

R6.text: Express a multiplicative relationship between two quantities as a ratio or fraction

R7.text: Understand and use proportion as equality of ratios

R8.text: Relate ratios to fractions and to linear functions

R9.text: Percentages and percentage change as fractions/decimals, multiplicatively; percentage of an amount; percentage increase/decrease; original value problems; simple interest

R10.text: Solve problems involving direct and inverse proportion, incl. graphical and algebraic representations

R11.text: Use compound units: speed, rates of pay, unit pricing, density, pressure

R12.text: Compare lengths, areas and volumes using ratio; links to similarity (incl. trigonometric ratios) and scale factors

R13.text: X inversely proportional to Y ≡ X proportional to 1/Y; construct and interpret equations for direct and inverse proportion

R14.text: Interpret gradient of a straight line as a rate of change; recognise graphs of direct and inverse proportion

R15.text: Gradient at a point as instantaneous rate of change; average and instantaneous rates (chords and tangents) in numerical, algebraic and graphical contexts

R16.text: Set up, solve and interpret growth and decay problems, incl. compound interest and general iterative processes

G1.text: Use conventional terms and notations (points, lines, vertices, edges, planes, parallel/perpendicular, polygons...); draw diagrams from written description

G2.text: Ruler and compass constructions (perpendicular bisector, perpendicular from/at a point, angle bisector); construct figures and solve loci problems

G3.text: Angles at a point/straight line, vertically opposite, alternate and corresponding angles; angle sums of triangles and polygons

G4.text: Properties and definitions of special quadrilaterals (square, rectangle, parallelogram, trapezium, kite, rhombus) and triangles

G5.text: Use the basic congruence criteria for triangles (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS)

G6.text: Apply angle facts, congruence, similarity and quadrilateral properties to derive results (incl. Pythagoras) and obtain simple proofs

G7.text: Identify, describe and construct congruent and similar shapes on coordinate axes via rotation, reflection, translation and enlargement (incl. fractional/negative scale factors)

G8.text: Describe changes and invariance achieved by combinations of rotations, reflections and translations

G9.text: Identify and apply circle definitions and properties: centre, radius, chord, diameter, circumference, tangent, arc, sector, segment

G10.text: Apply and prove the standard circle theorems and use them to prove related results

G11.text: Solve geometrical problems on coordinate axes

G12.text: Identify properties of faces, surfaces, edges and vertices of cubes, cuboids, prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres

G13.text: Construct and interpret plans and elevations of 3D shapes

G14.text: Use standard units of measure and related concepts (length, area, volume/capacity, mass, time, money)

G15.text: Measure line segments and angles; interpret maps and scale drawings; use of bearings

G16.text: Formulae for area of triangles, parallelograms, trapezia; volume of cuboids and right prisms (incl. cylinders)

G17.text: Circumference 2πr = πd and area πr²; perimeters; areas of circles and composite shapes; surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids

G18.text: Calculate arc lengths, angles and areas of sectors of circles

G19.text: Apply congruence and similarity, incl. relationships between lengths, areas and volumes in similar figures

G20.text: Pythagoras' theorem a² + b² = c² and trigonometric ratios; right-angled and general triangles in 2D and 3D

G21.text: Exact values of sin θ and cos θ for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°; of tan θ for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°

G22.text: Sine rule a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC and cosine rule a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A

G23.text: Area = ½ab sin C for area, sides or angles of any triangle

G25.text: Add/subtract vectors, multiply by a scalar; diagrammatic and column representations; use vectors to construct geometric arguments and proofs

P1.text: Record, describe and analyse frequency of outcomes using tables and frequency trees

P2.text: Apply randomness, fairness and equally likely events to calculate expected outcomes

P3.text: Relate relative expected frequencies to theoretical probability; the 0-1 probability scale

P4.text: Probabilities of an exhaustive set of outcomes/mutually exclusive events sum to one

P5.text: Empirical unbiased samples tend towards theoretical probability distributions with increasing sample size

P6.text: Enumerate sets and combinations systematically using tables, grids, Venn diagrams and tree diagrams

P7.text: Construct theoretical possibility spaces for single and combined experiments; calculate theoretical probabilities

P8.text: Probability of independent and dependent combined events, incl. tree diagrams; underlying assumptions

P9.text: Calculate and interpret conditional probabilities using two-way tables, tree diagrams and Venn diagrams

S1.text: Infer properties of populations/distributions from a sample; know the limitations of sampling. Higher-tier guidance includes capture–recapture.

S2.text: Interpret and construct tables, charts and diagrams: frequency tables, bar charts, pie charts, pictograms, time series graphs

S3.text: Construct and interpret diagrams for grouped discrete and continuous data: histograms (equal/unequal intervals) and cumulative frequency graphs

S4.text: Interpret, analyse and compare distributions: graphical representation incl. box plots; measures of central tendency (median, mean, mode, modal class) and spread (range, outliers, quartiles, IQR)

S5.text: Apply statistics to describe a population

S6.text: Use and interpret scatter graphs; correlation (not causation); lines of best fit; interpolation/extrapolation and their dangers
